chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from Abī Shibl, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Whoever loves you for what you are upon will enter Paradise, even if he does not say as you say.”

key_terms.أَحَبَّكُمْ: loved you; held sincere affection and devotion toward you
key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise; the abode of reward in the Hereafter
key_terms.عَلَىٰ مَا أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ: for what you are upon; because of your true path or religious stance
key_terms.كَمَا تَقُولُونَ: as you say; in the same way that you express it
key_terms.لَمْ يَقُلْ: did not say; did not express verbally

ai.seo_question: Can someone enter Paradise by loving the followers of truth even if they do not express the same beliefs exactly?
ai.summary: This hadith states that loving the believers for the truth and path they uphold is a cause for entering Paradise. It indicates the spiritual significance of sincere attachment and loyalty, even if a person does not fully articulate the same beliefs in the same manner.
